name: Nicaragua
headline: Nicaragua: +4.9% growth in 2025, 2.1% inflation, debt 35% of GDP
sections: Nicaragua is a $22.2 billion economy (2025), the world's 131st-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +4.9% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $9,284 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 12.6% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 2.1% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 10.5% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 2.7% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 9.5% (2025).
Gross government debt is 35% of GDP (2025), a low level that has fallen from 49% in 2020. The general government balance is +3.5% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is +9.5% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Trade equals 96% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 6.8% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 27% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 75.1 years (2024). Population: 6.7 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
